statements.venue: Written statement to Alaska's News Source
statements.quote: clear safeguards around the highest-risk AI technologies
statements.context: The station asked Alaska's congressional delegation whether they support guardrails on AI, after a campaign in Washington warning that AI could end human life; the article says Sullivan said these safeguards "are needed".
statements.reason: He says the highest-risk AI technologies need clear safeguards, which acknowledges serious risk in general terms, but he names no harm, so this sits between C and D.

statements.context: The same statement on AI guardrails, continuing directly after the call for safeguards.
statements.reason: This is about competition with China, which the rubric places at D.

statements.quote: these technologies, in which we are in a race with China in terms of their development, might determine who controls the entire 21st century between the United States and China.

statements.reason: He treats AI as a race with China and names no risk from AI itself.

grade_reason: His only remark found that touches risk from AI itself is a written statement that clear safeguards around the highest-risk AI technologies are needed. It names no harm, so C is a borderline call and a reviewer could reasonably choose D.
notes: The C quote is a fragment: the article quotes only those seven words and supplies "are needed" in its own voice, so the full sentence he wrote is not available. The statement date is the article's publication date (16 September 2026 Alaska time; the link shows 17 September); the statement itself may be a day or so earlier. The Congressional Record quote was read from the PDF, with line-break hyphens removed ("tech-nologies", "develop-ment"); his China and AI remarks begin on page S1037, and the link opens the PDF starting at S1036. Paraphrases left out: the article says he commended the Trump administration's 20 March 2026 National Policy Framework for AI (I could not find his own statement on his Senate site); a lobbying firm's summary says he raised concerns at a 2025 Senate Commerce hearing about US investment in Chinese AI (not opened). 23 September 2026 China letter: the two pages I opened (Commerce Committee Democrats release, WJLA report) do not list the 17 signers and do not mention Sullivan; coverage calls it a Democratic letter, so nothing shows he signed. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act: sources name Sanders and Casar as sponsors and some House cosponsors; nothing shows Sullivan co-sponsoring, and I did not check congress.gov. Two of the required searches (general AI statement, superintelligence) failed on a rate limit and the superintelligence one was rerun successfully with different wording; the session's search budget then ran out, so coverage is thinner than intended, in particular no dedicated search of hearing transcripts or of his campaign site. Fragments of his statement match the article text exactly, including curly quotation marks in the original, which are not reproduced inside the quotes here.
